activities.name: PR #1019 — refactor(daemon): move daemon into root package and remove MCP

activities.name: Issue #1008 — MCP: date-only or naive as_of crashes context_resolve/context_search
activities.summary: TypeError: can't subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes — passing as_of='2024-06-01' to the MCP read tools crashes the whole read.
activities.description: Filed 2026-07-13 by Aditya Painuli against potpie v2.0.0 on macOS, labelled bug. Four-hop chain: `_parse_as_of_iso` (adapters/inbound/mcp/server.py:51) only special-cases the `Z` suffix so `datetime.fromisoformat('2024-06-01')` returns a naive datetime; readers pass it straight through as `TaskContext(now=req.as_of)` (application/readers/_common.py:51); `RankingService.rank` keeps a caller-supplied `now` as-is (domain/ranking.py:120); `_recency` then subtracts it from tz-aware `valid_at` and raises. Counter-test: the same instant as `2024-06-01T00:00:00Z` works. Fixed by PR #1009. Search: offset-naive offset-aware, as_of date only, context_resolve TypeError, recency scoring crash.

activities.description: Filed 2026-07-06 by Nihit Gupta against potpie v2.0.0b3. Different task descriptions return the same claim set; the header prints `intent=feature confidence=low` with no classification performed; questions like 'what changed recently in the auth service?' return zero timeline items because the feature intent does not include timeline retrieval; and `confidence=low` is coverage-based, so it appears even when results are highly relevant. Asks for real detection, a neutral `unknown` fallback, and a visible signal of how the intent was selected. Addressed by PR #1006. Search: intent detection missing, default intent feature, zero timeline results, confidence low always.

activities.name: Issue #994 — Graph read CLI flags accepted but ignored on default read path
activities.summary: --repo, --query, --scope, --format table, --detail and --relations are accepted but never applied, so scoped reads are cosmetic on the default backend.
activities.description: Filed 2026-07-06 by Bharath Kumar K, closed 2026-07-14 by his own PR #995. Timeline `--repo`/`--query` do not change output; preferences `--scope repo:/path:/service:` does not narrow; unknown `--scope` keys pass silently; scoped runs still print a project-wide banner. The impact is stated precisely in the report: false negatives (users think there is no data when a filter would have matched) and false positives (users think scope narrowed results when it did not). Search: flags ignored, filter not applied, silent no-op flag, scoped read, graph read --scope, timeline recent --repo.

activities.name: Issue #992 — Domain errors and ok:false JSON exit 0 — automation cannot detect CLI failures
activities.summary: potpie --json cloud status prints code:not_implemented and exits 0; potpie --json graph status prints ok:false and exits 0, so shell chains treat failures as success.
activities.description: Filed 2026-07-06 by Nihit Gupta against potpie v2.0.0b3. The report includes a table: `cloud status` → `not_implemented` → exit 0; `graph status` → `ok:false` (e.g. `ambiguous_pot`) → exit 0; `graph nudge --event bogus` → `ok:false` → exit 0; and `potpie --json cloud status && echo "should not print"` prints anyway. Parser and usage errors behave correctly (`potpie pot create` → exit 2), so the gap is strictly domain-level failures. Addressed by PR #993. Search: exit code 0 on failure, CI cannot detect error, shell && chain, ok:false success exit, automation contract.

activities.name: Issue #981 — Fix mislabeled feature claims in potpie resolve output
activities.summary: PROVIDES and IMPLEMENTED_IN claims surface under the infra_topology include label instead of features, so output labels contradict claim semantics.
activities.description: Filed 2026-06-30 by Nihit Gupta, severity low/cosmetic, reproduced on a populated pot containing both infrastructure-topology and feature claims against the local graph backend. Expected: `infra_topology` returns only DEPENDS_ON, USES, DEPLOYED_TO, DEFINED_IN, HOSTED_ON and OWNED_BY, while PROVIDES and IMPLEMENTED_IN return under `features`; actual output prints lines like `[infra_topology] repo provides feature X`. Root cause is the top-level resolve path letting feature predicates flow through the infra_topology include. Related to the reader rework in #999. Search: wrong include label, feature claim under infra_topology, predicate categorization, resolve output labels.

activities.name: Issue #978 — Add next actions after potpie source add repo for empty pots
activities.summary: source add repo succeeds into an empty pot with no follow-up guidance, leaving users with an empty graph and no idea what to do next.
activities.description: Filed and closed 2026-06-30 by Nihit Gupta. The report is careful to affirm the design — source registration is intentionally registration-only and must not auto-trigger ingestion — and asks only for a next-actions block plus `recommended_next_action` in the JSON payload when the target pot has 0 claims. Suggested actions: inspect linked pots, switch to a populated pot, start a manual graph mutation workflow. Delivered by PR #972 together with #971. Search: empty graph after setup, nothing ingested, no next step, registration only, onboarding dead end.

activities.name: Issue #977 — service logs gives a generic 'no log file' for embedded graph backends
activities.summary: potpie service logs falkordb_lite returns {"lines": []} / 'no log file' because the backend runs embedded in the daemon, with no pointer to potpie daemon logs.
activities.description: Filed 2026-06-30 by Shambhavi Shinde, closed 2026-07-01 by PR #943. Root cause: `service logs` only checks `<home>/logs/service-<name>.log` and emitted a bare empty response when that path was missing, giving the same vague answer for `embedded`, `in_memory` and the `falkordblite` alias. The requested response shape — `status: embedded_backend`, `profile`, `recommended_log_command`, `database_path`, human `message` plus `detail` lines — is spelled out in the issue and is what shipped. Search: no log file, empty logs, falkordb_lite embedded, daemon logs, where is the database file.

activities.name: Issue #973 — `pot create --repo .` not registering the current repo
activities.summary: pot create <name> --use --repo . creates a source with name='.' and location=null and never sets the repo-local default, unlike source add repo .
activities.description: Filed 2026-06-29 by Shambhavi Shinde, closed 2026-07-01 by PR #974. Two divergent code paths: `source add repo` calls `resolve_repo_location()` + `add_source(location=...)` + `set_repo_default()`, while `pot create --repo` had `LocalPotStore.create()` append an inline `{kind: repo, name: repo}` with no location and no default (local_pot_store.py:85-92). Consequences listed in the issue: repo pot resolution breaks, `source list` shows unusable metadata, users must re-run source add manually, automation cannot treat the two as equivalent. Search: location null, repo default missing, pot create repo flag, source registration mismatch.
